title: Cosmic rays studied with a hybrid high school detector array
extended_summary:
This paper describes a hybrid detector setup for cosmic ray research that also serves education and outreach purposes in Dutch high schools. The authors present the LORUN/NAHSA system, which combines radio antennae and particle detectors to detect air showers from very high energy cosmic rays in coincidence. The project is framed as a pathfinder to extend cosmic ray detector arrays on high school buildings while giving students hands-on experience with scientific instrumentation.

The intervention/approach is not an instructional study in the usual sense, but a technology-and-outreach implementation in which high school students helped set up particle detectors on school buildings and the system was linked to university-based radio antennas. The setting is the Netherlands, primarily Nijmegen, where the NAHSA high school array triggered LORUN observations. The paper explains the hardware, triggering, data acquisition, and offline analysis pipeline used to match radio and particle signals.

The main results are engineering/observational rather than educational outcomes. The authors report three candidate cosmic ray events detected between January and August 2005, showing that the hybrid system worked as intended. They conclude that the setup demonstrates the feasibility and educational potential of combining radio and particle detection at high schools, and argue that additional development could eventually make such hybrid arrays more broadly available to high school students.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a physics/astronomy pathfinder report on cosmic ray detector hardware and student participation, not an education intervention study. It contains no evaluative methodology relevant to K-12 instructional technology, teacher feedback/coaching, or subgroup comparisons.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no measured educational impact, teacher outcome, or school-context effect reported. The paper only notes outreach and student involvement in building detectors, without evidence of learning or coaching outcomes.
